## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** on a tmux server that has never had theme colours stamped into it, the change works as described. With a ghostty or kitty client attached, `window-style`/`window-active-style` stay `default`, no OSC palette reaches the panes, and tmux draws default-colour cells as default (SGR 49/39), so the terminal's reloaded colours and opacity apply. The cursor-colour fallback, `COLORFGBG` and environment sync still run, and a `xterm-256color` client alone (the `TERM` Omarchy sets for foot and alacritty) gets the same full push as before. The new `test/cli` assertions fail on the base and pass on the head.

One issue remains: the skip path leaves colours stamped by earlier runs in place, and those earlier runs are common in normal use.

### Earlier stamps survive, so panes show the previous theme

Both stamped layers are persistent tmux state. The global `window-style`/`window-active-style` last until the server restarts or they are unset, and the per-pane OSC 10/11/4 palette lasts until the pane is reset or closed (tmux 3.7c `input.c`, `tty.c`). The head skips new writes but never clears old ones. Stamping still happens:

- on any tmux server that was running when the theme was changed with the current script (upgrade);
- on a theme change while tmux is detached, which is the normal state after closing the window in the `tmux attach || tmux new -s Work` flow (`bin/omarchy-launch-terminal-tmux`, `default/bash/aliases`), because no client means the full push runs;
- on a theme change while only a non-matching client (foot, alacritty) is attached.

The next theme change from ghostty or kitty then leaves every pane on the previous theme, while the terminal around tmux switches. Reproduced on a private tmux 3.7c server with synthetic themes A (bg `#102030`) and B (bg `#405060`):

| Sequence, then switch to theme B | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Clean server, ghostty client attached | `window-style` B, panes emit B bg (opaque, correct colour) | `window-style` default, panes emit default colours (fix works) |
| Theme A set while detached, ghostty attaches, then B | panes emit B | `window-style` still A, all panes emit A bg and fg, including a pane created after the stamp |
| Theme A set by the current script (upgrade), then B | panes emit B | panes emit A |

**Impact:** existing tmux users get the wrong theme in every pane, text colour included, and it stays opaque. On the detached path, transparency is lost again after each theme change made while tmux has no client. For those users this is worse than the base, which is opaque but shows the correct colours.

**Suggested change:** when the skip path runs, clear what earlier runs stamped instead of only skipping new writes: reset each pane's colours (`OSC 104`, `OSC 110`, `OSC 111`) and unset the global styles (`tmux set-option -gu window-style`, `-gu window-active-style`). On tmux 3.7c the order matters: `OSC 104` clears the pane palette but does not mark the pane's cached colours as stale, so an `OSC 110`/`OSC 111` or a style change has to follow it. Unsetting the styles after the pane writes returned every pane to default colours in the private tmux test. To avoid removing a `window-style` a user set deliberately in `tmux.conf`, unset only when the value still matches what the script last wrote (for example, recorded in a tmux user option). How ghostty renders after this reset was not observed on screen.

### One server-wide decision, made at theme-change time

`tmux_clients_reload_config` returns true if any attached client matches, and both skipped settings apply to the whole server. With a ghostty client and a foot client attached (possibly to different sessions), neither gets the push. The check also depends only on `TERM`.

**Impact:** after an earlier all-foot sync, foot panes on a mixed server keep the previous theme's stamped colours (the finding above). On a server with no earlier stamps, foot's own theme hook may still supply the new colours; that was not checked on screen. A user `TERM` override in ghostty or kitty turns the fix off, and a remote ghostty client reached over SSH counts as self-reloading even though it does not reload this machine's theme.

**Suggested change:** addressing the stale-state finding removes most of the mixed-client impact. Mentioning the any-client rule in the function comment would make the server-wide scope explicit.

**Scope note:** alacritty also reloads its own config and by default applies opacity only to default-background cells, but Omarchy gives it `TERM=xterm-256color`, so it keeps the full push. Behaviour for alacritty is unchanged from the base, and transparent alacritty panes remain affected.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head and base, plus tmux 3.7c, ghostty 1.3.1, kitty 0.48.2 and alacritty 0.17.0 source at the versions Arch ships. The PR's tmux test block was run in isolation on base and head. A private tmux 3.7c server with Omarchy's `tmux.conf`, pty clients using `xterm-ghostty`, `xterm-kitty` and `xterm-256color`, and synthetic themes recorded tmux options, pane colours and the SGR colours tmux sent to each client. No GUI terminal was run, so on-screen rendering in ghostty, kitty, foot and alacritty was not observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
